h: Liverpool climbing tips and a waterfront finish
p: There's something about Clip 'n Climb that brings out everyone's competitive side, and in Liverpool that's saying something. Expect plenty of banter on the race walls, a bit of trash talk at the bottom of the jumps, and a lot of laughing when the loudest one in the group suddenly goes very quiet at the top.

A bit of planning makes the whole day flow. Every climber needs a participation form, with a parent or guardian signing for under-18s. Get it done online before you leave home and you'll skip the queue at the desk. Read the age guidance when booking, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and rules on supervising little ones.

Allow a couple of hours for your visit. That leaves time for arrival, harness fitting and the safety briefing, plus a breather afterwards. Eat light beforehand and bring water, because it's harder work than it looks.
A climbing technique tip: push with your legs rather than heaving with your arms. Your forearms will thank you, and you'll manage more walls in your session.

When you're done, head to the waterfront. The Museum of Liverpool and the Merseyside Maritime Museum are both free and packed with stories of the city and its port. A Mersey Ferries cruise across the river gives you a classic view of the famous skyline from the water. If you'd prefer greenery, Sefton Park in the south of the city is huge, with a lake and the Victorian Palm House.
